questions.question: Which method provides a distributed database that is used to resolve FQDNs to an IP address?
questions.explanation: Domain Name Services (DNS) is a distributed database of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) to IP addresses.

questions.question: What statement is correct about forward lookups?
choices: Forward lookups resolve FQDNs to IP addresses.
Forward lookups resolve IP addresses to FQDNs.
A forward lookup forwards a request to another DNS server.
Forward lookups resolve IP addresses from the queried DNS server, without the help of other DNS servers.
questions.explanation: Forward lookups resolve fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) to an IP address.

questions.question: Which protocol and port number does DNS use for direct queries?
questions.explanation: Domain Name Services direct queries are performed over the UDP protocol to port 53. The queries do not require the TCP setup and teardown because the queries are simple request and reply messages, so UDP is used for direct queries.

questions.question: Which statement describes FQDNs?
choices: FQDNs are significant from right to left, starting with a period for the root.
FQDNs are always registered with a registrar.
FQDNs are significant from left to right, starting with a period for the root.
A DNS server always processes the entire FQDN.
questions.explanation: Fully qualified domain names are significant from right to left, starting with a period to signify the root. The period is normally not visible on the FQDN, but it is processed as the root lookup.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about reverse lookups?
choices: A reverse lookup is the resolution of an FQDN to an IP address.
A reverse lookup is when the DNS queried can answer the request without asking another DNS server.
A reverse lookup is when the request needs to be reversed to another DNS server.
A reverse lookup is the resolution of an IP address to FQDN.
questions.explanation: A reverse lookup is when the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) is resolved from an IP address. This is useful when you want to identify an IP address. From the IP address, you can derive the FQDN.

questions.question: Which record type is used for an IPv4 address to FQDN for DNS queries?
questions.explanation: The PTR, or pointer record, is used to look up IP addresses and return FQDNs that are mapped to them. This is helpful to identify an IP address, and in the case of SSH, it is used to positively identify the host you are connecting to.

questions.question: What gets appended to hostname queries for DNS resolution?
questions.explanation: The configured DNS domain name is appended to the hostname query. As an example, if you query a hostname of routera and the configured domain name is network.local, the DNS server will see a query for rotuera.network.local.

questions.question: Which is the most secure method of name resolution for routers and switches?
questions.explanation: Static hostname entries are the most secure name resolution method for routers and switches. This is because the switch or router does not need to forward-query a server. However, static hostname entries are not scalable.

questions.question: Which type of DNS record holds the IPv4 IP address for a hostname?
questions.explanation: The A record is the DNS record that is queried when you want to resolve a hostname to an IP address.

questions.question: What limits the amount of time that a DNS entry is available in DNS cache?
questions.explanation: The time to live, or TTL, limits the amount of time in which a DNS entry will be available in the DNS cache. The TTL can be defined by the DNS administrator on the entry, or it can be defined in the SOA record as the default TTL.

questions.question: Which is an alternative to DNS lookup on routers?
questions.explanation: The alternative to DNS lookup on routers is configuring static hostname entries. This method unfortunately is not scalable.

questions.question: Which record type is used for IPv6 hostname lookup for DNS queries?
questions.explanation: The Quad-A (AAAA) record type is used for IPv6 hostname lookup on DNS servers.

questions.question: Which protocol and port number is used for DNS domain zone transfers?
questions.explanation: The protocol TCP and port number 53 are used for DNS domain zone transfers. UDP port 53 is used for iterative queries, since the message is short. However, zone transfers require the help of TCP because there is more information than there is in a query.

questions.question: What is a reason to configure DNS on a router or switch?
choices: ACLs can dynamically reverse hostnames to IPs.
Configuration allows ease of administration from the router or switch when connecting to other devices by FQDN.
Configuration allows access to the router or switch by the FQDN.
Configuration allows secure communications via HTTPS.
questions.explanation: Configuring DNS on a router or switch allows for ease of administration from the router or switch. It enables DNS resolution from the console. It does not enable DNS resolution from external sources unless you have configured the hostnames on the DNS server.

questions.question: You are were trying to type the ping command into the router and mistype it and receive the output of Translating "png". . . domain server (255.255.255.255) , which halts you from continuing. Which command will stop this behavior?
questions.explanation: By default, all routers and switches are set for ip domain-lookup. Because no IP address is set, the router or switch will try to broadcast the DNS query. If you configure no ip domain-lookup , the query will just fail, and you will not need to break out of it.

questions.question: Which command will set the resolution of a host so that DNS does not need to be used for resolution?
questions.explanation: The command ip host routerb 10.1.2.3 will configure the local resolution of the host routerb to an IP address of 10.1.2.3.

questions.question: Which command will configure the router or switch to use a specific DNS server for hostname lookups?
questions.explanation: The command ip name-server 172.16.1.5 will configure the router or switch to query the DNS server of 172.16.1.5 for hostname lookups. You can specify multiple DNS servers by using a space as a delimiter between each name for fault tolerance.

questions.question: Which command will configure the domain name to append to a DNS query?
questions.explanation: The command ip domain-name sybex.com will set the appended domain name of sybex.com for DNS queries. This command will allow the proper FQDN to be resolved by DNS.

questions.question: What is at the end of all FQDN addresses?
questions.explanation: A period is always appended to all FQDNs. This is significant because it represents the root, where all DNS resolution begins. The root or period is not often visible, but it is part of the DNS recursion process.

questions.question: When configuring the name server(s) for domain lookup, what is a best practice?
choices: Always use a mixture of public and private DNS servers for fault tolerance.
questions.explanation: A best practice for security is to always use a trusted DNS server. This is normally a server under the control of the enterprise, so it is a private DNS server.

questions.question: Which command will help verify the hostnames that are statically configured?
questions.explanation: The command show hosts will allow you to verify the statically configured hosts.

questions.question: Your DNS administrator has changed the DNS entry for RouterB. You clear the DNS cache and ping routerb.sybex.com again but still ping the original address. All other DNS addresses work fine. What is the problem?
choices: The DNS administrator made an error.
The router is configured to the wrong DNS server.
The domain name of the router is incorrect.
RouterB has a host entry configured.
questions.explanation: If the cache is cleared after the change has been made to DNS and you still get the same IP address, the reason is most likely that there is a host entry configured. The command s how running-configuration will show you if there is an entry.
questions.topic: 5.2 Troubleshoot client connectivity issues involving DNS

questions.question: You have configured a router to point to the DNS server with the IP address 10.2.2.2 and configured the domain name of sybex.com. However, you cannot resolve the host routerb .sybex.com. Which Windows command will help you verify DNS name resolution?
questions.explanation: The command nslookup routerb.sybex.com will allow you to positively verify name resolution. Ping should not be used because the failure of ICMP echo will make the command fail, giving you a false result.
questions.topic: 5.2 Troubleshoot client connectivity issues involving DNS

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the DNS server you are using for name resolution?
questions.explanation: The command to verify DNS server(s) configured for name lookup is show running-configuration . The line to look for in the output is ip name-server x.x.x.x.
questions.topic: 5.2 Troubleshoot client connectivity issues involving DNS

questions.question: You have configured the domain name of sybex.com and the DNS server 10.2.3.4 on a router. However, after you type ping routerb , the console promptly returns “% Unrecognized host or address or protocol not running.” What is wrong?
questions.explanation: Options A, B, and C will return the error ““% Unrecognized host or address or protocol not running.”
questions.topic: 5.2 Troubleshoot client connectivity issues involving DNS

questions.question: Your DNS administrator has changed the DNS entry for RouterB. You ping routerb.sybex .com again, but still ping the original address. All other DNS addresses work fine. What is the problem?
choices: The router’s DNS cache needs to be cleared.
The router is configured to the wrong DNS server.
The domain name of the router is incorrect.
The DNS administrator made an error.
questions.explanation: DNS changes can be made on-the-fly. However, the results will not be seen immediately unless all cache is cleared and routers request the new address. The problem would be that this router had resolved routerb.sybex.com already and the entry still exists in the cache, which needs to be cleared.
questions.topic: 5.2 Troubleshoot client connectivity issues involving DNS

questions.question: Which command will remove the entry routerb.sybex.com out of the DNS cache or a switch without affecting the rest of the cache?
questions.explanation: The command to clear only the host routerb.sybex.com from the DNS cache is clear host routerb.sybex.com . This will remove only that particular host from the cache.
questions.topic: 5.2 Troubleshoot client connectivity issues involving DNS

questions.question: Which statement is true about the Discover packet of DHCP?
choices: The layer 3 source is a link-local address of the client.
The layer 2 destination is the MAC address of the DHCP server.
The layer 2 source is the MAC address of the client.
The layer 3 destination is a unicast to the DHCP server.
questions.explanation: The DHCP Discover packet is a broadcast to discover a DHCP server. The layer 3 packet and layer 2 frame are broadcasts. Since the client does not have an IP address yet, the layer 3 source address is all zeros. However, the layer 2 source MAC address is filled out in the frame.
questions.topic: 5.3 Configure and verify DHCP on a router (excluding static reservations)

questions.question: Which command will configure a router to use DHCP for IP address assignment?
questions.explanation: The command ip address dhcp will configure the router to use DHCP for IP address assignment. This command needs to be issued on the interface in which you want the IP address to be configured, similar to static IP address assignment.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the IP address assigned to a router’s interface?
questions.explanation: The command show ip interface will display the IP addresses configured on the router’s interfaces. It will detail which are static and which have been allocated through DHCP.

questions.question: Which port and protocol does the client use for DHCP messages?
questions.explanation: The DHCP client uses the source port UDP/68 to await connections back from the server. It keeps this protocol and port open in an active state until DHCP is complete.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the active DHCP server that has assigned an IP address to the router?
questions.explanation: The command show dhcp lease will help you verify the IP address configured on the router, the DHCP server that served the lease, and the lease time in seconds.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the Offer packet of DHCP?
choices: The layer 3 source is a link-local address of the client.
The layer 3 destination is a unicast to the DHCP client.
The layer 2 destination is the MAC address of the DHCP client.
The layer 2 source is the MAC address of the server.
questions.explanation: The DHCP Offer packet is a broadcast packet from the DHCP server to the DHCP client. The layer 3 packet and layer 2 frame are both broadcasts.
questions.topic: 5.3 Configure and verify DHCP on a router (excluding static reservations)

questions.question: Which command will configure a DHCP relay agent on an interface to the DHCP server of 10.10.1.101?
questions.explanation: The command ip helper-address 10.10.1.101 will configure the interface to become a DHCP relay agent. This command must be configured on the interface in which you want the DHCP relay agent to listen and respond.

questions.question: Which DHCP field helps a DHCP server decide which scope to serve to the DHCP relay agent?
questions.explanation: The Gateway Address (GIADDR) field is filled out by the DHCP relay agent before the DHCP packet is sent to the DHCP server. This field helps the DHCP server decide which scope to send an Offer message back for.

questions.question: Which port and protocol does the server use to await connections for DHCP?
questions.explanation: The DHCP server bind port of UDP/67 is used for awaiting connections from DHCP clients.

questions.question: Which Windows command will allow you to see the DHCP server that has configured the client computer with an IP address?
questions.explanation: The command ipconfig /all will display the generic information of IP, subnet mask, and gateway. It will also display the DHCP server that configured the client with an IP address.

questions.question: Which message is sent from the DHCP client to the DHCP server to confirm the offer of an IP address?
questions.explanation: The DHCP acknowledgment message is sent from the DHCP client to the DHCP server to acknowledge that the IP address offered will be used by the client.

questions.question: What form of communications does a DHCP client use to initially acquire an IP address?
questions.explanation: DHCP uses layer 3 broadcasts by sending packets to 255.255.255.255 for initial DHCP discovery.

questions.question: At what point of the lease time will the client ask for a renewal of the IP address from the DHCP server?
questions.explanation: DHCP clients request a renewal of the lease halfway through the lease time of the IP address.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about the DHCP process?
choices: The DHCP server is responsible for maintaining the life cycle of an IP address.
The DHCP client is responsible for maintaining the life cycle of an IP address.
DHCP uses multicasting between the client and server.
The DHCP lease is negotiated between client and server.
questions.explanation: After the initial Discover, Offer, Request, and Acknowledge, it is the client’s responsibility to maintain the lease of the IP address. This includes release and renewal.

questions.question: Which transport protocol does DHCP use?
questions.explanation: DHCP uses UDP as a connectionless protocol for the Discover, Offer, Request, and Acknowledge packets.
questions.topic: 5.3 Configure and verify DHCP on a router (excluding static reservations)

questions.question: Which command will allow you to diagnose DHCP relay agent messages on a router or switch?
questions.explanation: The command debug ip dhcp server packet will show the details of a DHCP relay agent conversation. It will detail conversation between the client and router and the router and the DHCP server.

questions.question: What is DHCPv6 used for when a network is configured for Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC)?
choices: Stateless configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing
Configuration of clients with the IPv6 network IDs
Configuration of clients with IPv6 options
Stateful configuration of clients for IPv6 addressing
questions.explanation: Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC) allows for the client to learn the network ID and calculate a host ID that is unique. However, SLAAC is lacking the ability to configure options such as DNS time servers, etc. DHCPv6 allows for the configuration of these options when used in conjunction with SLAAC.
questions.topic: 5.3 Configure and verify DHCP on a router (excluding static reservations)

questions.question: The DHCP server in the network went down. What happens to clients that have obtained IP addresses from the DHCP server?
choices: They lose their IP address after one-half of their lease has expired.
They lose their IP address after their entire lease has expired.
They lose their IP address immediately.
They lose their IP address after seven-eighths of their lease has expired.
questions.explanation: They will lose their IP after their entire lease has expired. Until the lease expires, they will have functioning IP addresses.

questions.question: Which command will configure a router as a DHCPv6 relay agent for a stateful DHCPv6 server?
questions.explanation: The command ipv6 dhcp relay destination 2001:db8:1:2::2 will configure the router interface to relay DHCP requests to 2001:db8:1:2::2. This command must be configured on the interface that is to listen for DHCPv6 requests.

questions.question: You need to configure a lease duration of 4 hours for a DHCP pool. Which command will achieve this?
questions.explanation: The command lease 0 4 0 will configure the DHCP pool for a duration of 0 days, 4 hours, and 0 minutes.

questions.question: Which command will create an exclusion of 192.168.1.16 to 192.168.1.31 in the DHCP pool?
questions.explanation: The command ip dhcp exclusion-address 192.168.1.16 192.168.1.31 will configure an exclusion address range by specifying the low IP address and the high IP address. This command is configured from the global configuration prompt.

questions.question: When configuring a DHCP pool, which option(s) will configure the client to boot from a PXE server?
questions.explanation: The command option 66 ip 10.1.1.5 sets the TFTP server to boot from. The command bootfile boot\x86\wdsnbp.com sets the bootfile on the TFTP server to boot\x86\wdsnbp.com . Some clients may need other options, such as option 60, which is the vendor class identifier.

questions.question: Which command will configure the default gateway option for a DHCP pool?
questions.explanation: The default gateway option is configured under the DHCP pool with the command default-router 10.1.1.1 . This will set the default gateway to 10.1.1.1 for the DHCP clients.

questions.question: Which option will configure the DNS servers for the DHCP clients?
questions.explanation: The DNS server is configured with the command dns-server 10.1.1.5 . This command is used in lieu of the option command so that multiple DNS servers can be configured on the same line.

questions.question: Which command will configure a DHCP pool to serve the IP addresses for 192.168.1.0/24?
questions.explanation: The command network 192.168.1.0 255.255.255.0 will configure the network ID and subnet mask required for DHCP.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about stateful DHCPv6?
choices: Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID and host ID.
Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID, host ID, and default router.
Stateful DHCPv6 works in conjunction with SLAAC.
questions.explanation: Stateful DHCPv6 supplies the network ID and host ID. The default router is discovered through the Neighbor Discovery Protocol.
questions.topic: 5.3 Configure and verify DHCP on a router (excluding static reservations)

questions.question: Which command will configure a router interface to obtain its IP address via a stateful DHCPv6?
questions.explanation: The command ipv6 address dhcp will configure the interface to obtain its IP address via stateful DHCPv6.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the IPv6 configuration for stateful DHCPv6?
questions.explanation: The command show ipv6 dhcp interface will display which mode the client is in, the address, and the DHCP Unique Identifier (DUID) as well as the stateful DHCPv6 server address.

questions.question: What happens if you delete a current lease on the DHCP server?
choices: The server will offer the IP address to another node, at which time the original client will relinquish the IP address.
The server will offer the IP address to another node, which will cause a duplicate address.
The server will contact the client to immediately relinquish the IP address.
The client will immediately renew its lease for the current IP address.
questions.explanation: When the lease for a node is deleted on the DHCP server, the DHCP server is free to hand out the lease to another node. This happens independently from the client, as there is no communication from server to client about the lease. The client will retain the IP address until the renewal period, which will cause a duplication of IP addressing.
questions.topic: 5.4 Troubleshoot client-and router-based DHCP connectivity issues

questions.question: What happens at the client when the lease for an IP address reaches seven-eighths of the lease cycle?
choices: Nothing. The DHCP client will retain the lease.
The DHCP client will renew its lease.
The DHCP client will relinquish the use of the IP address.
The DHCP client will perform a DHCP rebinding.
questions.explanation: At seven-eighths of the lease cycle, the DHCP client will perform a rebinding. The rebinding process means that the original DHCP server was down at the one-half mark of the lease, so now the client will try to rebind with any responding DHCP server.

questions.question: Which command is used on a router to request a renewal lease on a DHCP interface?
questions.explanation: The command renew dhcp gi 0/0 will force the DHCP client to renew the current lease.

questions.question: How are nodes and leased IPs tracked in the DHCP bindings table on a switch or router?
questions.explanation: When the DHCP server issues an IP address to a client, it records the MAC address in the DHCP bindings table. This is recorded along with the lease expiration.

questions.question: During the DHCP rebinding, which message is sent from the client?
questions.explanation: During the DHCP rebinding process, a DHCP Request is sent. However, it is not sent to the originating server since rebinding occurs after the renewal period was missed. So the DHCP Request is broadcast to any listening DHCP server.

questions.question: You have configured a DHCP server on a router interface. You test a Windows client and receive the address 169.254.24.56. What can you conclude?
choices: The DHCP server is not configured properly and the client has configured itself with a link-local address.
The client had a static IP address of 169.254.24.0/24 configured.
The DHCP server is configured for APIPA.
You have successfully configured the scope of 169.254.24.0/24.
questions.explanation: The DHCP server is not configured properly. When a Windows client configures itself with an IP address of 169.254. x.x , it is using APIPA, or Automatic Private IP Addressing (link-local addressing).
questions.topic: 5.4 Troubleshoot client-and router-based DHCP connectivity issues

questions.question: What mechanism is used by DHCP clients to avoid IP address conflicts with other DHCP clients?
questions.explanation: DHCP clients use a protocol called Gratuitous Address Resolution Protocol (GARP). The GARP packet is a broadcast to the other clients in the network. If no response is heard, there are no conflicts.
questions.topic: 5.4 Troubleshoot client-and router-based DHCP connectivity issues

questions.question: What happens when a router or switch detects a duplicate IP address for a DHCP process?
choices: The IP address is removed from the DHCP pool.
The IP address is still served to the client.
The DHCP will serve the IP address in the future.
questions.explanation: When DHCP detects a duplicate IP address in the pool, it will remove the duplicate IP address from the DHCP pool and place it into the conflict table. It will require manual intervention to reserve the IP address.
questions.topic: 5.4 Troubleshoot client-and router-based DHCP connectivity issues

questions.question: Before you configure the DHCP pool and network, which option should you configure?
questions.explanation: It is recommended that you create an exclusion for the router interface and any statically configured hosts in the network for the DHCP pool. This will prevent duplicate IP address conflicts.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to check if the router or switch handed out a duplicate IP address?
questions.explanation: The command show ip dhcp conflict will display the IP address conflicts on the router or switch. The table will display how the conflict was discovered with GARP or Ping as well as the detection time.
questions.topic: 5.4 Troubleshoot client-and router-based DHCP connectivity issues

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see the current utilization of the DHCP pools configured?
questions.explanation: The command show ip dhcp pool will allow you to see the current utilization of the scopes configured on the router.

questions.question: How can an address be removed from the DHCP conflict table?
questions.explanation: The command to remove an IP address from the conflict table is clear ip dhcp conflict 192.168.1.6 . This command will remove a single IP address of 192.168.1.6 from the table and place it back in the DHCP pool. Alternatively, all of the conflicts can be cleared with an * in lieu of the IP address.
questions.topic: 5.4 Troubleshoot client-and router-based DHCP connectivity issues

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the current DHCP leases on a router or a switch?
questions.explanation: The command show ip dhcp bindings will allow you to verify all of the current DHCP leases served by the router or switch.

questions.question: Which protocol is an IEEE standard that is supported openly as a first hop redundancy protocol (FHRP)?
questions.explanation: Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) is an IEEE open standard that is supported freely on many router products.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: In the MAC address 0000.0c07.ac0a, what is the well-known Hot standby Router Protocol (HSRP) ID?
questions.explanation: The well-known HSRP ID is 07.ac. Anytime you see the 07.ac in the second part of the MAC address along with the Cisco OUI, you can identify that HSRP is being employed.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which protocol is a Cisco Proprietary protocol for load-balancing routers?
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP) is a Cisco Proprietary protocol that supports redundancy and per-subnet load balancing.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: In the MAC address 0000.0c07.ac01, what is the HSRPv1 group number?
questions.explanation: The HSRP group number in the MAC address 0000.0c07.ac05 is 01. After the Cisco OUI and well-known HSPR ID, the last two digits are the HSRP group identifier.

questions.question: What is the default priority of HSRP?
questions.explanation: The default priority of HSRP is 100.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of HSRPv1 groups that can be created?
questions.explanation: You can create up to 256 HSRP groups on a router. This would include group 0 to 255 for a total of 256 groups.

questions.question: Which port and protocol are used by HSRP for communications?
questions.explanation: HSRP routers communicate with each other on port 1985 using UDP.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which statement is correct about HSRP?
choices: HSRP allows for per-packet load balancing.
The virtual router sends hello packets to the HSRP group.
All routers in an HSRP group are active.
Only one router in an HSRP group can be active.
questions.explanation: Only one router can be active at a time in an HSRP group. All other routers are standby routers, until the active router fails.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: What type of communication is used between HSRP members?
questions.explanation: HSRP uses multicasting to communicate among HSRP group members. For HSRPv1, the address is 224.0.0.2, and for HSRPv2, the address is 224.0.0.102.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: When a host sends an outgoing packet to an HSRP group, which router provides the destination address for the default gateway?
questions.explanation: The virtual router is responsible for host communications such as an ARP request for the host’s default gateway. Technically, this is served by the active router since it is hosting the virtual router. However, it is the virtual router’s IP address and MAC address that are used for outgoing packets.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which timer must expire for a standby router in an HSRP group to become the active router?
questions.explanation: The hold timer must expire for the standby router to become an active router. The hold timer is three times the hello timer, so three hello packets must be missed before the standby becomes active.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which port and protocol are used by Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP) for communications?
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP) use the port number 3222 and the protocol UDP for router communications.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which is a difference between HSRPv1 and HSRPv2?
choices: HSRPv1 uses broadcasts, and HSRPv2 uses multicasts.
HSRPv2 does not use hello packets.
questions.explanation: HSRP version 2 allows for timers to be configured in milliseconds in lieu of seconds. This allows for quicker failover between active and standby routers.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP)?
choices: The active virtual gateway will respond with a MAC address of an active virtual forwarder.
The virtual router is responsible for responding to tracking requests.
The active router is responsible for responding to clients with the virtual router’s MAC address.
The active virtual gateway will respond with a MAC address of the active router.
questions.explanation: The active virtual gateway (AVG) is responsible for responding to ARP requests from hosts. The AVG will reply with the MAC address of any one of the active virtual forwarders (AVFs).
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which router is elected to become the GLBP active virtual gateway?
choices: The router with the lowest priority and lowest IP address
The router with the highest priority
The router with the lowest priority
The router with the highest priority and highest IP address
questions.explanation: The router with the highest priority will become the AVG. However, if all routers have the same priority, then the router with the highest IP address configured becomes the tiebreaker.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: How many active virtual forwarders are supported per the Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP) group?
questions.explanation: Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP) supports up to four active virtual forwarders per GLBP group.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which command will allow Router B to always become the active router for HSRP?
questions.explanation: The command standby 1 priority 150 will set the HSRP group of 1 on this router to a priority of 150. As long as all other routers are set to the default of 100, this router will become the default router on the next election.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of Hot Standby Router Protocol version 2 groups that can be created?
questions.explanation: You can create up to 4,096 HSRP groups on a router. This would include group 0 to 4096 for a total of 4,096 groups.

questions.question: Your company is running a first hop redundancy protocol (FHRP). You notice that the MAC address of the default gateway is 0000.0c9f.f123. Which FHRP is being employed?
questions.explanation: Hot Standby Router Protocol version 2 (HSRPv2) is being employed. It uses an OUI of 0000.0c and a well-known identifier of 9f.f, and the last three digits identify the HSRP group, which has been expanded from two digits in version 1.

questions.question: What is the definition of preemption for Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP)?
choices: When a standby router comes online, it allows for a re-election of the active router.
It ignores the priorities of the routers and elects an active router by highest IP address.
It allows the protocol to effectively load-balance per packet.
It watches an upstream interface and fails over when the interface goes down.
questions.explanation: Preemption allows for the election process to happen for a newly added HSRP router. If preemption is not enabled, then the newly added HSRP router will become a standby router.

questions.question: Which is a method of configuring Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP) so that traffic is not directed to one router?
choices: Configure version 2 for all HSRP groups.
Configure PPPoE on the router interfaces.
Configure all routers in the HSRP as active routers.
Configure an HSRP group per VLAN and alternate the priority above 100.
questions.explanation: Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP) allows for only one active router per HSRP group. However, you can configure multiple VLANs with HSRP groups. You can then alternate a higher-than-default priority to force an active router per VLAN. This will give you a rudimentary way of balancing traffic.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to verify the state of the current router for HSRP?
questions.explanation: The command show standby will allow you to verify the state of the current router for HSRP.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: You have just changed the priority on Router A to 150. All other routers have the default priority. What is wrong?
choices: The HSRP group is not set for preemption.
The hold timer is set too high and needs to timeout.
Router A has too low of an IP address.
questions.explanation: The HSRP group is not set for preemption, which is the default behavior for HSRP. You need to enable preemption, which will allow a reelection when the priority is changed or if a new standby router comes online. If preemption is disabled, the active router will have affinity.

questions.question: Which command will allow you to enable preemption for HSRP?
questions.explanation: The command standby 1 preempt will configure HSRP group 1 for preemption. This command must be configured under the interface on which HSRP has been enabled. The command show standby will allow you to verify this.

questions.question: Which command will configure VRRP on an interface with an IP address of 10.1.2.3?
questions.explanation: The command vrrp 1 ip 10.1.2.3 will configure the interface with VRRP with a virtual IP address of 10.1.2.3.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which command from the host will allow you to see the router your packets have been routed with?
questions.explanation: The command tracert 10.1.2.33 will allow you to see the real IP address on the router that is responding for the ICMP packet. With HSRP, the virtual MAC address is returned for the virtual IP address of the default gateway. However, when ping is used the ping packet enters the real interface, and then the interface responds with the real IP address.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see real-time diagnostics of HSRP?
questions.explanation: The command debug standby will allow you to see real-time information from HSRP on the router on which you have entered the command.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which statement is correct about GLBP?
choices: The active virtual gateway will respond with a MAC address of the active router.
GLBP allows for per-host load balancing.
GLBP allows for per-subnet load balancing.
The virtual router is responsible for responding to tracking requests.
questions.explanation: GLBP allows for per-host load balancing. It does this by allowing the active virtual router to respond for the virtual IP address. The AVG then hands out the MAC address in the ARP request for one of the active virtual forwarders. It does this in a round-robin fashion.
questions.topic: 5.5 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot basic HSRP

questions.question: Which command will allow you to set the hello and hold timer for HSRPv2 to a hello of 200 milliseconds and a hold of 700 milliseconds?
questions.explanation: The command standby 1 timers msec 200 msec 700 will set the HSRP group of 1 with a hello timer of 200 milliseconds and a hold timer of 700 milliseconds. This is configured inside of the interface in which the HSRP group was created.

questions.question: Which method will allow you to use RFC 1918 addresses for Internet requests?
questions.explanation: Network Address Translation (NAT) was created to slow the depletion of Internet addresses. It does this by translating RFC 1918 privatized addresses to one or many public IP addresses. It allows the packets to masquerade as the public IP address on the Internet until is it translated back to the private IP address.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which is a disadvantage of using NAT?
questions.explanation: Network Address Translation creates packet switching path delay. This is because each address traveling through the NAT process requires lookup time for the translation.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which type of Network Address Translation is used for one-to-one mapping between local and global addresses?
questions.explanation: Static Network Address Translation is a one-to-one mapping between a local (private) and global (public) IP address. This is used for servers, such as web servers and email servers, so that they are Internet reachable.

questions.question: Which type of Network Address Translation is used for one-to-one mapping (sometimes called many-to-many) on the fly between local and global addresses that are allocated from a pool of addresses?
questions.explanation: Dynamic Network Address Translation is a one-to-one mapping on the fly in which the IP address is allocated from a pool of addresses. This is often called many-to-many. When a host makes an attempt to go through the NAT process, an IP address is mapped to the host from the global pool. This type of NAT is useful in network address overlap situations because there is less latency than NAT Overloading.

questions.question: Which type of Network Address Translation is used for a many-to-one translation in which the source and destination ports are tracked?
questions.explanation: Network Address Translation overloading, sometimes called Port Address Translation, allows for one public IP address to be used for NAT. The conversations between local and global IPs are sorted using the source and destination ports for the various applications. This is the most common NAT and can be found in any home, small office, or enterprise.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about static NAT?
choices: Static NAT has less latency than dynamic NAT.
Static NAT is less secure than dynamic NAT.
The translation is always present in the NAT table.
The translation is never present in the NAT table.
questions.explanation: Static NAT translation entries are always present in the NAT table. Static NAT entries have the same amount of security and latency as dynamic NAT.

questions.question: Network Address Translation overloading is also called what?
questions.explanation: Network Address Translation overloading is also called Port Address Translation. This is because a single IP address can allow up to 65,535 simulations inside local connections, which are segregated in the NAT table by source and destination port number.

questions.question: What is an advantage of Network Address Translation?
choices: Decreased utilization of public IP addresses
questions.explanation: A decrease in public IP address utilization is a direct benefit of using NAT. Memory utilization will increase, latency of packets will increase, and some network applications could have problems with NAT.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which is a practical application of static Network Address Translation?
choices: Internet access for an enterprise from private IP addressing
Publishing a web server on the Internet from a private IP address
questions.explanation: Static NAT is mainly used for publishing internal resources on the Internet, Such services are email servers, web servers, collaboration servers, and so on.

questions.question: Which term describes the IP address of the internal host before NAT?
questions.explanation: The inside local address is “inside” the enterprise and under “local” control of the enterprise. This term is from the perspective of the NAT device.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage to using Port Address Translation?
choices: Lower memory usage than other NAT types
questions.explanation: The flexibility of Internet connections is usually a driving factor for PAT (NAT Overloading). Memory is significantly higher with PAT, since the source and destination port numbers must be recorded in the NAT table. There is no effect on packet loss, and jitter is marginally affected.

questions.question: Which command would you configure on the private network interface for NAT?
questions.explanation: The command to configure the private side of the network interface for NAT is ip nat inside . This command is configured on the interface in which you want to define it as the “inside” of your network.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which command will allow you to view the NAT translations active on the router?
questions.explanation: The command show ip nat translations will allow you to view the active NAT translations on the router.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which command will allow you to view the current number of active NAT translations on the router?
questions.explanation: The command show ip nat statistics will allow you to view the number of active NAT translations on the router. In addition, it will provide you with the current inside and outside interfaces.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: When configuring dynamic NAT, why must you configure an access list?
choices: The access list allows incoming access from outside global addresses.
The access list allows outgoing access from outside local addresses.
The access list allows outgoing access from inside local addresses.
The access list allows outgoing access from inside global addresses.
questions.explanation: The access list allows the inside local address to pass through the NAT process.

questions.question: Which command will wipe out all current NAT translations in the NAT table?
questions.explanation: The command clear ip nat translation * will clear all IP NAT translations out of the NAT table. The asterisk is used as a wildcard for all addresses. You can alternatively specify a specific inside or outside NAT address.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: What happens to host communications when the NAT table is manually cleared?
choices: Established TCP sessions will need to reestablish and will not disturb communications.
Established UDP sessions will need to reestablish and will disturb communications.
Established TCP sessions will need to reestablish and will disturb communications.
No disturbance in communications will be observed.
questions.explanation: When the NAT table clears, established TCP sessions will need to reestablish via the three-way handshake. This creates a problem for some secure protocols such as SSH, which will drop the established connection and not reestablish a new connection. UDP does not have a state to its connection, so little or no disturbance will be seen.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see real time Network Address Translations?
questions.explanation: The command debug ip nat will allow you to see real-time NAT translations. When you issue this command, you should know that each NAT translation will log to the screen or logging server and will spike CPU usage.
questions.topic: 5.6 Configure, verify, and troubleshoot inside source NAT

questions.question: Which protocol helps synchronize time for routers and switches?
questions.explanation: The Network Time Protocol (NTP) is used to synchronize time for routers and switches.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Why is time synchronization important for routers and switches?
choices: It is important for serialized communication frame alignment.
It helps delivery of packets via timed queues.
It is important for quality of service queuing.
It is important for logging accuracy.
questions.explanation: Time synchronization is important for logging accuracy. Serial communication frame alignment is timed via DCE clocking and packet queues are timed by how fast they can respond.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which command will allow your router to synchronize with a time source of 129.6.15.28?
questions.explanation: The command ntp server 129.6.15.28 will configure your router to connect to the server 129.6.15.28 as an NTP source. This command must be entered in global configuration mode.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which command configures the router or switch to trust its internal time clock?
questions.explanation: The command ntp master configures the router or switch to trust its internal time clock.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which command will allow you to see if the router or switch is using NTP?
questions.explanation: The command show clock detail will result in either no time source or time source is NTP if the router or switch is configured to slave off a server for time.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which command will allow you to view the time details from a configured server?
questions.explanation: The command show ntp associations detail will allow you to view the NTP clock details from the master NTP server.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which protocol and port does NTP use for time synchronization?
questions.explanation: The Network Time Protocol uses UDP port 123 for time synchronization.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which command will help you diagnose if the router or switch is getting an answer back from an NTP server?
questions.explanation: The command debug ntp packets will allow you to verify packets received from an NTP server.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which is a best practice for setting up NTP?
choices: Always configure the time source to a DNS address.
Configure all devices as master servers.
Configure all devices to different NTP servers for redundancy.
Configure all devices to a public NTP server.
questions.explanation: A best practice is to configure the main router in your network to a known good trusted time source by its DNS address. All devices in your network should then be configured to point to this trusted router. All time sources should pyramid out from the central source of time in your network.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode

questions.question: Which command will allow you to view the time drift observed by NTP?
questions.explanation: The command show ntp status will allow you to see the current time source, the precision of the time source, and the drift from your internal time clock.
questions.topic: 5.7 Configure and verify NTP operating in a client/server mode
